# package aggregate

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/server/aggregate"
```

Package aggregate calculates the standard Aggregates of OPC 10000-13 (Part 13 §5.4) over the raw values of a Variable: every Aggregate of Part 13 §5.4.3 but AnnotationCount, with the interval rules of §5.4.2, the bounding values of §3.1.8 and §3.1.9, the StatusCode calculation of §5.4.3.2 and the Aggregate bits of Part 4 §7.38.1 (Calculated, Interpolated, Partial, MultipleValues).

A [Request](#type-request) holds the time domain, the Aggregate and the [Config](#type-config); it is the ReadProcessedDetails of a HistoryRead (Part 11 §6.5.4) or the AggregateFilter of a MonitoredItem (Part 4 §7.22.4). [Request.Calculate](#func-request-calculate) returns one value per interval:

	r := aggregate.Request{
		Aggregate:          ua.NewNumericNodeID(0, id.AggregateFunctionTimeAverage),
		Start:              start,
		End:                end,
		ProcessingInterval: time.Minute,
		Config:             aggregate.DefaultConfig(),
	}
	from, to := r.Window(0, r.Intervals()) // the raw values to read
	values, status := r.Calculate(raw)

The server uses the package for the processed reads of its \*Historian and of any HistoryProvider that does not implement ProcessedHistoryReader: it reads the raw values of [Request.Window](#func-request-window) with ReadRaw and calculates. A custom provider therefore gets the Aggregates by implementing ReadRaw only, and their configuration by implementing AggregateConfigProvider.

The tests calculate every example of Annex A (the file AggregateExamples.csv of the OPC Foundation, pinned in schema/manifest.json) and compare each value, timestamp and StatusCode; where the file conflicts with a clause the clause is followed, and deviations\_test.go lists each such row with the clause.

## Constants

```go
const MaxIntervals = 1 << 20
```

MaxIntervals is the most intervals one Request may have. A request with more is Bad\_InvalidArgument: a client that needs them reads the range in several requests.

```go
const Resolution = time.Millisecond
```

Resolution is the time resolution of the calculations: the EffectiveEndTime is "the time immediately before endTime where the time resolution of the Server determines the exact value", and "If there is one data point in the Interval and it falls on the StartTime the time duration used in calculations is one unit of the time resolution of the Server" (Part 13 §3.1.3, §5.4.2.4). It is one millisecond, the resolution of the examples of Annex A.

## Functions

### func Description

```go
func Description(aggregateType *ua.NodeID) string
```

Description returns the Description of a supported AggregateFunction Object, the "en" text of Part 13 Table 5, "" for one the package does not calculate.

### func Functions

```go
func Functions() []*ua.NodeID
```

Functions returns the NodeIds of the AggregateFunction Objects (Part 13 §4.2.2) the package calculates, in the order of Part 13 §5.4.3. It holds every standard Aggregate but AnnotationCount (§5.4.3.20), which counts the Annotations of Part 11 §5.1.2 rather than values.

### func Name

```go
func Name(aggregateType *ua.NodeID) string
```

Name returns the BrowseName of a supported AggregateFunction Object (Part 13 §4.2.2.2, Table 5), "" for one the package does not calculate.

### func Supported

```go
func Supported(aggregateType *ua.NodeID) bool
```

Supported reports whether the package calculates the Aggregate of the AggregateFunction Object aggregateType.

## Types

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// TreatUncertainAsBad: "A value of True indicates the Server considers
	// the severity equivalent to Bad, a value of False indicates the Server
	// considers the severity equivalent to Good, unless the Aggregate
	// definition says otherwise" (Part 13 §4.2.1.2).
	TreatUncertainAsBad bool
	// PercentDataBad is "the minimum percentage of Bad data in a given
	// interval required for the StatusCode for the given interval for
	// processed data request to be set to Bad" (Part 13 §4.2.1.2).
	PercentDataBad uint8
	// PercentDataGood is "the minimum percentage of Good data in a given
	// interval required for the StatusCode for the given interval for the
	// processed data requests to be set to Good" (Part 13 §4.2.1.2).
	PercentDataGood uint8
	// UseSlopedExtrapolation selects SlopedExtrapolation over
	// SteppedExtrapolation where an Interpolated Bounding Value has no value
	// after it (Part 13 §4.2.1.2, §3.1.8). "For SimpleBounds this value is
	// ignored."
	UseSlopedExtrapolation bool
	// Stepped is the Stepped Property of the Variable: True for
	// SteppedInterpolation, False for SlopedInterpolation (Part 11 §5.2.2).
	// It changes the Aggregates that use Simple Bounding Values and the
	// time weighted ones that follow it (TimeAverage2, Total2, ...).
	Stepped bool
}
```

Config is the configuration an Aggregate is calculated with: the Properties of the AggregateConfigurationType (Part 13 §4.2.1.2) and the Stepped Property of the HistoricalDataConfigurationType of the Variable (Part 11 §5.2.2).

#### func DefaultConfig

```go
func DefaultConfig() Config
```

DefaultConfig is the default configuration: "The default value is True" for TreatUncertainAsBad, 100 for PercentDataBad and PercentDataGood, False for UseSlopedExtrapolation (Part 13 §4.2.1.2), and False for Stepped (Part 11 §5.2.2).

#### func (Config) AggregateConfiguration

```go
func (c Config) AggregateConfiguration() *ua.AggregateConfiguration
```

AggregateConfiguration returns c as the structure of the services, with useServerCapabilitiesDefaults false.

#### func (Config) Override

```go
func (c Config) Override(ac *ua.AggregateConfiguration) Config
```

Override returns the configuration a request asks for: the aggregateConfiguration of ReadProcessedDetails (Part 11 §6.5.4.1) or of an AggregateFilter (Part 4 §7.22.4) "allows Clients to override the Aggregate configuration settings supplied by the AggregateConfiguration Object". With useServerCapabilitiesDefaults, or without a configuration, c (the configuration of the Variable or of the Server) is used and "any values specified for the other parameters are ignored" (Part 13 §5.2.2). Stepped is a Property of the Variable and is kept.

A configuration with every field zero or false is read as no override: it is what a client that leaves the structure unset encodes, and as an override it is not valid (PercentDataGood 0 \< 100 - PercentDataBad 0) and would make every interval Bad\_AggregateInvalidInputs. UA-.NETStandard reads it the same way.

#### func (Config) Valid

```go
func (c Config) Valid() bool
```

Valid reports whether the percentages give a valid calculation: "The PercentDataGood and PercentDataBad shall follow the following relationship PercentDataGood ≥ (100 - PercentDataBad)" and neither may exceed 100 (Part 13 §4.2.1.2). A configuration that is not valid gives Bad\_AggregateInvalidInputs.

### type Request

```go
type Request struct {
	// Aggregate is the NodeId of the AggregateFunction Object (Part 13
	// §4.2.2), one of [Functions].
	Aggregate *ua.NodeID
	// Start and End are the startTime and the endTime. An End before Start
	// reads backwards: "If endTime is less than startTime then the data
	// shall be returned in reverse order with the later data coming first"
	// (Part 11 §6.5.4.2).
	Start, End time.Time
	// ProcessingInterval is the length of the intervals; 0 is one interval
	// from Start to End (Part 13 §5.4.3.1).
	ProcessingInterval time.Duration
	// Config is the AggregateConfiguration and the Stepped Property.
	Config Config
}
```

Request is the time domain and the Aggregate of a processed read (the ReadProcessedDetails of Part 11 §6.5.4) or of an AggregateFilter (Part 4 §7.22.4).

#### func (Request) Calculate

```go
func (r Request) Calculate(raw []*ua.DataValue) ([]*ua.DataValue, ua.StatusCode)
```

Calculate returns the processed value of every interval of the request, calculated over raw, the raw values of the Variable (any order): the values in the time domain of the request and the values before and after it that bounding values need, see [Request.Window](#func-request-window). The first and the last value of raw are taken as the start and the end of data: an interval before the first value is "Before Start of Data", one after the last value "After End of Data", and the last value is taken as the latest value of a history that is still collecting (Part 13 §5.3.3.2). The status is that of [Request.Check](#func-request-check).

#### func (Request) CalculateIntervals

```go
func (r Request) CalculateIntervals(raw []*ua.DataValue, first, last int) ([]*ua.DataValue, ua.StatusCode)
```

CalculateIntervals is [Request.Calculate](#func-request-calculate) for the intervals first to last-1 only.

#### func (Request) Check

```go
func (r Request) Check() ua.StatusCode
```

Check returns the operation result of a request that cannot be calculated, Good otherwise:

  - Bad\_AggregateNotSupported for an Aggregate this package does not calculate: "The requested AggregateFunction is not supported by the Server for the specified Node" (Part 13 §5.3.2, Table 45);
  - Bad\_InvalidArgument when Start or End is not given, Start equals End ("No intervals. Returns a Bad\_InvalidArgument StatusCode", Part 13 §5.4.2.2, Table 49), the ProcessingInterval is negative, or the request has more than MaxIntervals intervals;
  - Bad\_AggregateInvalidInputs for a Config that is not [Config.Valid](#func-config-valid) (Part 13 §4.2.1.2).

#### func (Request) Interval

```go
func (r Request) Interval(i int) (start, end time.Time)
```

Interval returns the start and the end of interval i in the direction of the request: \[start, end) forwards, and backwards from start to end "with the exception that the 'early time' is excluded from the interval and the 'late time' is included" (Part 13 §5.4.2.2).

#### func (Request) Intervals

```go
func (r Request) Intervals() int
```

Intervals returns the number of intervals of the request, 0 when it does not pass [Request.Check](#func-request-check).

#### func (Request) Window

```go
func (r Request) Window(first, last int) (from, to time.Time)
```

Window returns the time range of raw values intervals first to last-1 need, the values from before the first and after the last interval that the bounding values are found with included. A provider that is asked for an Aggregate it does not calculate itself reads its raw values of that range: "The period of time that is searched to discover the values before and after the timestamp is Server dependent ... The Server as a minimum should search a time range which is at least the size of the ProcessingInterval" (Part 13 §3.1.8, §3.1.9). The window reaches one ProcessingInterval, or the span of the request when that is 0 or longer, beyond the intervals on each side.
